newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich Court upholds UBS share plan.
newsitem.headline: Zurich Court upholds UBS share plan.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said the commercial court of Zurich had upheld the bank's plan to introduce a single bearer share and if no appeals against the ruling were filed within one month, the single share would be introduced "immediately."
UBS shareholders approved the move to adopt a single share on November 22, 1994, but it was prevented from taking effect by two suits calling for annulment.
One suit was filed by BK Vision, UBS's largest shareholder and part of Martin Ebner's BK Group, and the other by Peter Hafter, member of the board of BK Vision and private shareholder in UBS.
A spokesman for BK Vision said it was too early to comment on whether an appeal would be filed.
He said BK Vision had only just received the 124-page ruling earlier today.
"If BK Vision doesn't appeal, then it is all over and we intend to introduce a single share immediately," a UBS spokeswoman said in response to inquiries.
BK Vision and Hafter have 30 days to file an appeal.
